note: Short-form manifest for The Festie Bible. Every beat is copied from the book's own scenario fields; no line is written here. Regenerate rather than hand-editing.
caveat: Unlike The Pattern Decoder, this book has no disconfirming field -- nothing that names the innocent behaviour that looks the same. `move` and `truth` soften the read but are not a disconfirming case. Worth writing one before these ship at volume.

clips.name: The Festival Boyfriend / Instant Soul Sister

beats.scene: You met him at the silent disco Friday night and by Saturday breakfast he's saved your spot, got you coffee, and told his whole camp you're "the one." He keeps saying "we" — we should catch that set, we should stay toget
beats.tells: "I've never felt this way" before he knows your last name
beats.say: I'm feeling this energy — I also need to flow freely this weekend. Let's vibe without locking anything down.
beats.truth: Real connection can survive a slower pace. Anyone who can't wait is applying pressure, not offering magic.

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"R"CHECK: "Is this moving faster than I chose?" — if the speed is his, not yours, that's your first signal.
clips.move: Enjoy the spark. Let the pace be yours. A connection that's real will still be real after you check in with camp.
clips.dark_title: The Isolator

clips.name: False Brotherhood / Instant Tribe
clips.hook_line: BRO YOU'RE ONE OF US NOW

beats.hook: BRO YOU'RE ONE OF US NOW
beats.scene: You rolled in solo and by Friday night you're deep in a crew that feels like family.
beats.tells: Full adoption happens within hours — you're "family" before you've slept
beats.say: I'm not gonna hold anything for anyone — not my thing. Still down to hang though.
beats.truth: Real brothers don't put you at legal risk two days after meeting you. That's not family.

clips.check: B.A.S.S.—"S"CHECK: "When did I last actually talk to my own people — not this crew?"
clips.move: Enjoy the crew. Don't carry anything for people you've known less than a weekend. Full stop.
clips.dark_title: The Drug Mule Setup — This Is Real

clips.name: The Veteran Who Makes You Dependent

beats.scene: You're overwhelmed at the gate — it's bigger than you imagined and your signal is patchy.
beats.tells: Makes himself the essential navigator of your experience from the first hour
beats.say: Thanks for showing me around — can you point me toward the Harm Reduction tent so I know where it is?
beats.truth: A real guide makes you less dependent on them over time. Watch for that.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "V" CHECK: "Can I get to my camp, the medical tent, and the exit right now without asking him? If not —...
clips.move: Accept genuine help. Build your own navigation as fast as possible. Independence is the goal.
clips.dark_title: Build Your Own Map In The First Two Hours

clips.name: Fetishization Dressed as Acceptance
clips.hook_line: YOU ARE SO BEAUTIFUL AND FREE

beats.hook: YOU ARE SO BEAUTIFUL AND FREE
beats.scene: "I have always been so drawn to queer energy — there is something so free and authentic about it." She says it looking right at you and it feels like being seen.
beats.tells: Their interest centers your identity category rather than you as a specific person
beats.say: I appreciate the curiosity — I am actually pretty private about that stuff. Tell me about you.
beats.truth: You are a person, not an experience. Anyone who cannot tell the difference does not deserve access to you.

clips.check: P.R.I.D.E. — "P" CHECK: "Is this person interested in me specifically — or in what I represent to them?"
clips.move: Receive genuine interest warmly. Notice when interest shifts from you as a person to you as a category. Name it or leave.
clips.dark_title: When Straight Curiosity Becomes Predatory

clips.name: The Exposure Promoter

beats.scene: "We can't pay for the live painting but your work will be seen by 20,000 people this weekend and we'll tag you in everything — this could really launch you." You spend 16 hours creating something extraordinary on their m
beats.tells: Payment replaced with "exposure," "experience," or future opportunity — all unquantifiable
beats.say: I'd love to be involved — my rate for a live painting is [X]. What's your budget?
beats.truth: Your art is your labor. Your labor has a price. You get to know what it is.

clips.check: C.R.E.A.T.E. — "C" CHECK: "Is there a written agreement — or just a verbal promise that evaporates after the event?"
clips.move: Know your rate before every conversation. Exposure is a supplement, not a replacement.
clips.dark_title: The Live Painting Minimum Contract

clips.name: The Promoter Who Books and Controls

beats.scene: "I'm building something with your sound specifically in mind — I need you for three dates this summer and if those go well we're talking main stage next year.
beats.tells: Future opportunity always slightly out of reach — dependent on your continued compliance
beats.say: I'm excited about these dates — let's get the agreement in writing so we're both protected. I can send my standard rider tonight.
beats.truth: Any promoter who won't put it in writing is showing you what the deal actually is.

clips.check: S.O.U.N.D. — "S" CHECK: "Is there a signed contract — or just a verbal promise and a sense that questioning it risks...
clips.move: No contract, no soundcheck. This is a full sentence and a complete policy.
clips.dark_title: The Minimum Performance Contract

clips.name: The Bait-and-Switch Promoter

beats.scene: The pitch was perfect: high-foot-traffic spot near the main stage, 2,000 attendees, electricity included.
beats.tells: Placement promises made verbally — not written into the vendor agreement
beats.say: I would love to participate — can you send me the vendor agreement with placement details and all fees before I commit?
beats.truth: A great pitch that is not in writing is just a story.

clips.check: M.A.R.K.E.T. — "M" CHECK: "Is the placement, the attendance number, and every fee in writing — or just verbally...
clips.move: If it is not in the written agreement it does not exist. Pay only what the paper says.
clips.dark_title: Vendor Agreement Must-Haves

clips.name: The Attendee Who Romantically Targets Staff on Duty

beats.scene: You have been doing back-to-back shifts at the Harm Reduction tent and you are tired but still fully present with everyone who comes in.
beats.tells: Multiple visits to your station with escalating personal rather than service-related conversation
beats.say: "I am on shift right now so I keep things professional during my role — I hope you have a great rest of your festival."
beats.truth: Your caregiving presence is a professional skill. Not everyone who benefits from it is entitled to more of you.

clips.check: H.O.L.D. — "H" CHECK: "Am I maintaining the boundary between my care role and my personal availability?"
clips.move: Maintain the on-duty boundary. Warm, caring, and professionally boundaried are completely compatible.
clips.dark_title: The On-Duty Boundary — Why It Exists

clips.name: When Your Care Energy Becomes a Hook
clips.hook_line: YOU ARE SO SAFE TO BE AROUND

beats.hook: YOU ARE SO SAFE TO BE AROUND
beats.scene: He has been to your tent three times today.
beats.tells: Multiple visits with escalating personal rather than support-related conversation
beats.say: "I am on shift right now so I keep things professional during my role — I hope you have a great rest of your festival."
beats.truth: Your care is a professional skill. Not everyone who benefits from it is entitled to more of you.

clips.check: C.A.R.E. — "C" CHECK: "Am I maintaining the distinction between my care role and my personal availability?"
clips.move: Warm, caring, professionally boundaried. All three at the same time. That is the standard.

clips.name: Camp Recruitment and What It Signals

beats.scene: You recruited twelve new members this season.
beats.tells: New members doing disproportionate labor compared to senior members without discussion
beats.say: "I want to do a camp culture check-in before the festival — I want to hear honestly from everyone about how things are going."
beats.truth: You cannot protect your camp from dynamics you are not willing to look at.

clips.check: L.E.A.D. — "L" CHECK: "What dynamics in my camp am I avoiding looking at because things are running well overall?"
clips.move: Look honestly at the dynamics you have been avoiding. The health of your camp depends on what you are willing to see.
clips.dark_title: Camp Health Self-Assessment

clips.name: Promising What You Cannot Deliver

beats.scene: You pitched a vendor on a premium spot near the main stage, 2,000 attendees, electricity included.
beats.tells: Attendance numbers and traffic projections should be accurate and from the current event context
beats.say: "Here is what our event actually delivered last year and what we are realistically planning for this year."
beats.truth: The reputation you are building is the one that is accurate — not the one in your pitch.

clips.check: E.V.E.N.T. — "V" CHECK: "Would I be comfortable if every vendor and artist I have worked with saw this pitch in...
clips.move: Represent your event accurately in every agreement. Every time. That is the baseline.
clips.dark_title: What Honest Representation Looks Like

clips.name: Hydration, Electrolytes, and Heat Safety

beats.scene: It is 2pm Saturday and it is hot.
beats.tells: Drink water consistently throughout the day — at least 500ml per hour in heat and while dancing
beats.say: Hey — when did you last have water? Come on, let us both drink something right now.
beats.truth: Every medical tent at every festival sees preventable heat illness every day. Do not be that story.

clips.check: S.A.F.E. — "F" CHECK: "Do I know where the medical tent is — and have I actually had enough water in the last hour?"
clips.move: Drink water now. Take an electrolyte packet. Find shade for ten minutes. Do it before you need to.
clips.dark_title: Heat Stroke Is A Medical Emergency

clips.name: The Gifter With a Ledger

beats.scene: She covered your wristband at the gate when your card declined.
beats.tells: Gifts arrive before any actual friendship — fast, often in front of witnesses
beats.say: That was genuinely kind — thank you. I'm gonna find my camp. Catch you at the main stage.
beats.truth: In real gifting culture the gift is complete the moment it leaves your hand. Anyone who picks it back up was never giving.

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"O"CHECK: "Am I still connected to my actual people — or has dependency on her replaced that?"
clips.move: Receive kindness warmly. Leave freely. Gratitude is a feeling — not a transaction that purchases your loyalty.
clips.dark_title: When The Gift Is The Substance

clips.name: Sexual Reciprocity Trap / Predatory Women

beats.scene: She zeroed in on you Saturday afternoon — beautiful, forward, electric.
beats.tells: Sexual attention and financial asks arrive in the same package
beats.say: I'm tapped out for covering things this weekend — still down to hang though.
beats.truth: Desire is real. Desire being used as a lever is also real. You're allowed to notice both.

clips.check: B.A.S.S.—"A"CHECK: "Who has access to my wallet and decisions right now — and what do they actually want?"
clips.move: Enjoy connection. Watch whether things actually flow both ways. Money in one direction is a pattern, not a moment.
clips.dark_title: Spiking Happens To Men — Not Rare

clips.name: Pedestal Ploy / The Special Exception

beats.scene: "Most people who come for the first time don't get it like you do.
beats.tells: "You're not like other first-timers" — your natural peer group gets gently dismissed
beats.say: That means a lot — I'm gonna go check in with the people I came with. See you at the set tonight.
beats.truth: The people who came with you are your actual family this weekend. Don't let flattery move you away from them.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "E" CHECK: "This person is still a stranger. Warmth and flattery are not the same thing as safety."
clips.move: Receive the compliment. Stay with your people. Specialness that requires isolation isn't specialness.
clips.dark_title: Your First-Timer Peer Group Is Your Greatest Asset

clips.name: Allyship as Access / Performative Safety

beats.scene: He has the progress pride flag on his tent.
beats.tells: Their allyship is loud and demonstrative — performed for an audience rather than lived quietly
beats.say: I appreciate that — I am going to take my time getting to know people this weekend.
beats.truth: Real allyship is behavior. Anyone can learn the vocabulary. Watch what they do.

clips.check: P.R.I.D.E. — "R" CHECK: "Does this person's behavior match their stated values — or is the language the whole...
clips.move: Watch behavior over time. Real allyship is consistent and quiet. Loud, demonstrative allyship deserves more scrutiny, not less.
clips.dark_title: What Real Allyship Looks Like In Practice

clips.name: The Collab That Becomes Unpaid Labor

beats.scene: "I have this incredible vision — I can see it so clearly — I just need someone with your skills to bring it to life.
beats.tells: They bring concept or personality; you bring skill, time, materials, and execution
beats.say: I'm into the idea — let's talk about what each of us is actually bringing so we're clear on credit before we start.
beats.truth: Equal credit requires equal contribution. Concepts and execution are not the same thing.

clips.check: C.R.E.A.T.E. — "A" CHECK: "Does my name appear clearly on this work in a way that reflects my actual contribution?"
clips.move: Define the contribution split before you start creating. If they can't have that conversation — that's your answer.
clips.dark_title: Photo And Video Credit — Non-Negotiable

clips.name: Predatory Management / The Isolation Manager

beats.scene: She approached you after a set that went off.
beats.tells: Discourages direct relationships with bookers, labels, promoters — "let me handle it"
beats.say: "I appreciate you handling things — I also keep direct relationships with my bookers. That's just how I work."
beats.truth: A manager who needs to be your only industry contact needs to be your former manager.

clips.check: S.O.U.N.D. — "N" CHECK: "Can I talk directly to my booker or label — or does everything go through them first?"
clips.move: Maintain direct relationships with at least 3 industry contacts independently of any manager. Always.
clips.dark_title: Management Contract Basics

clips.name: Terms Shifted After You Are Fully Committed

beats.scene: You confirmed spot 14 near the main entrance with electrical hookup in writing two months ago.
beats.tells: Material terms change after full payment and you are completely committed
beats.say: This placement does not match our agreement. I am setting up under protest and will follow up in writing.
beats.truth: The paper trail you build before the event is the only thing that protects you at the event.

clips.check: M.A.R.K.E.T. — "R" CHECK: "Do I have written documentation of what was originally agreed so I can actually...
clips.move: Document the original agreement. Document every change. Respond to all changes in writing immediately.
clips.dark_title: When They Change Your Terms After Arrival

clips.name: Recruited Under False Premises / Scope Creep in Your Role
clips.clinical: Manufactured Dependency / Bait and Switch Role

beats.scene: The volunteer description said: two four-hour shifts managing crowd flow, accommodation provided, meals covered, full festival access.
beats.tells: The role as described and the role as experienced are materially different
beats.say: "I am excited to help — can you send me the written volunteer terms including schedule, accommodation, and meals before I confirm?"
beats.truth: Volunteer labor is still labor. It deserves clear terms and honest expectations.

clips.check: H.O.L.D. — "O" CHECK: "Is what I am being asked to do now what I agreed to do before I arrived?"
clips.move: Get your volunteer terms in writing before you commit. They are not asking too much. You are not asking too much.
clips.dark_title: Volunteer Agreement Basics Before You Commit

clips.name: When Someone Is Using the Space for Something Other Than Support
clips.hook_line: THE PARTICIPANT WHO RUNS A PATTERN

beats.hook: THE PARTICIPANT WHO RUNS A PATTERN
beats.scene: He has been to the tent four times this weekend.
beats.tells: Multiple visits with shifting or evolving presentations of the support need
beats.say: I want to flag something I have noticed about a repeat visitor — can we talk privately for a minute?
beats.truth: Your care role requires discernment as much as compassion. Both are part of doing it well.

clips.check: C.A.R.E. — "R" CHECK: "Is the pattern of this person's engagement consistent with genuine support seeking — or...
clips.move: Trust the pattern. Note it. Share it with a colleague. Document it. That is what good safeguarding looks like.
clips.dark_title: Documenting Concerning Patterns

clips.name: When Someone in Your Camp Is Causing Harm

beats.scene: A newer member comes to you with a concern about someone who has been in the camp for four years.
beats.tells: A member with concerns is coming to you directly — this is the outcome of the trust you built
beats.say: Thank you for telling me. I am going to take this seriously. Here is what happens next.
beats.truth: The standard you set when it is hard is the only standard that matters.

clips.check: L.E.A.D. — "L" CHECK: "Am I responding to this in a way that protects the person who came to me — or the person...
clips.move: Believe enough to act. Document. Separate. Consult. Follow up. Make a decision. In that order.
clips.dark_title: Responding To Harm Reports In Your Camp

clips.name: Financial Accountability to Artists and Vendors

beats.scene: The event cost more than projected.
beats.tells: Post-event financial "adjustments" are contract violations — not conversations to negotiate
beats.say: "The payment will be in your account by [agreed date]. Let me know if you do not receive it by then."
beats.truth: Your financial reputation is built one payment at a time. It is also destroyed one payment at a time.

clips.check: E.V.E.N.T. — "T" CHECK: "Am I paying what I agreed, to whom I agreed, on the timeline I agreed — every time?"
clips.move: Pay what you agreed, on the agreed timeline. Every time. This is the whole standard.
clips.dark_title: What Professional Payment Practice Looks Like

clips.name: The Physical Infrastructure That Makes Everything Safer
clips.hook_line: FOOD, SLEEP, AND YOUR ACTUAL BODY

beats.scene: It is Sunday morning. You have slept a total of six hours over three nights.

beats.say: I am going to get a couple hours — wake me up for the set I marked. I will be more here for it if I sleep.
beats.truth: Rest is not missing the festival. Rest is what makes you available to actually be in it.

clips.move: Eat something real. Sleep when you can. Your experience of the festival depends on your body being functional.

beats.scene: "I never come to this stage. I had a vision in ceremony last month about a woman in a red hat and here you are." He's holding your hands.
beats.tells: Spiritual or cosmic language to explain why YOU specifically were chosen

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"V"CHECK: "Do I actually know this person — or just the character they're performing this weekend?"
clips.move: Let the feeling be real. Let the verification also be real. Destiny that's true is still true in three weeks.

beats.tells: Decision needs to happen RIGHT NOW — closing window, tonight only
beats.say: That sounds interesting — let me sleep on it and find you tomorrow if I'm in.
beats.truth: If it evaporates the moment you slow down, it was never real.

clips.check: B.A.S.S.—"A"CHECK: "Who actually has access to my financial decisions right now and what do I actually know...
clips.move: Any opportunity that requires a fast yes deserves a slow no. Real things survive 24 hours of verification.
clips.dark_title: Ticket Wristband Scams At The Gate

clips.name: The Substance Introduction Trap

beats.scene: "You've never tried it? Oh you HAVE to — this is literally what the festival is for.
beats.tells: Pressured or encouraged to try something new without informed consent and preparation
beats.say: "I appreciate the offer — I want to make sure I've got my setup right first. Can you help me find the Harm Reduction tent?"
beats.truth: Your first time is not something to be swept into. It's something to prepare for.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "V" CHECK: "Can I get to my camp, the medical tent, and the exit right now without asking him? If not —...
clips.move: Your first experience is yours to set the terms of. Test it, pace it, know your support.

clips.name: Assumed Community / The Instant Queer Family Trap
clips.hook_line: IT KNEW YOU WERE LIKE ME

beats.hook: IT KNEW YOU WERE LIKE ME
beats.scene: "We are queer fam — we look out for each other." She says it warmly and it lands in a real place because you know how much that community has meant in your life.
beats.tells: Shared identity invoked immediately as a basis for trust and obligation you have not established
beats.say: I appreciate the solidarity — I take my time getting to know people regardless. Tell me more about you.
beats.truth: Your queerness is yours. It does not obligate you to anyone who shares it.

clips.check: P.R.I.D.E. — "I" CHECK: "Am I giving this person more than I would give any other stranger because of shared...
clips.move: Let shared identity be a warm starting point. Let actual behavior be the basis for actual trust.
clips.dark_title: Community Solidarity Is Not Obligation

clips.name: The Connector Who Wants a Cut of Everything

beats.scene: "I'm going to connect you with everyone this weekend — I know all the right people." He does introduce you to two legitimate leads.
beats.tells: Introduces themselves as your "rep" or "manager" in conversations without your agreement
beats.say: "I appreciate the intros — I want to be clear that I'm handling my own arrangements. Any intros are just that — intros, not representation."
beats.truth: Anyone who represents themselves as your representative before you've agreed to that is telling you who they are.

clips.check: C.R.E.A.T.E. — "C" CHECK: "Have I agreed to any representation arrangement — or is someone claiming one that...
clips.move: Define every assistance relationship before it becomes a representation relationship.
clips.dark_title: Correcting False Representation

clips.name: The Bait and Switch Booking

beats.scene: "We're really excited to have you — you'll be on the Garden Stage, Saturday evening set, solid slot." You announce it, post it, your fans make plans.
beats.tells: Details confirmed verbally don't match the written confirmation when it arrives
beats.say: I'd love to announce this — can you send me the written confirmation with stage, set time, and fee first?
beats.truth: Your audience's excitement is yours. Don't let it become someone else's leverage.

clips.check: S.O.U.N.D. — "S" CHECK: "Have I confirmed every material detail of this booking in writing before I announce...
clips.move: Nothing gets announced until you have written confirmation of every material detail.
clips.dark_title: Announce Only After Written Confirmation

clips.name: The Camp Host Who Expects Inventory as Rent

beats.scene: The camp offered you a booth placement and a campsite.
beats.tells: Contribution expectations are vague at start and expand with each event
beats.say: I want to understand what the arrangement looks like financially before I commit — can we talk through what is expected specifically?
beats.truth: Community costs should be defined, mutual, and agreed to in advance. Anything else is uncompensated labor.

clips.check: M.A.R.K.E.T. — "E" CHECK: "What would it actually cost me to leave this arrangement — and is that cost getting...
clips.move: Calculate every camp arrangement in actual dollars before you commit to another event.
clips.dark_title: Calculate Your Actual Camp Arrangement Cost

clips.name: Bad Actors Who Target Safe Spaces
clips.hook_line: THE PREDATOR KNOWS WHERE THE TENT IS
clips.clinical: Position of Trust Exploitation / Predatory Access

beats.hook: THE PREDATOR KNOWS WHERE THE TENT IS
beats.scene: He has been volunteering in the Harm Reduction tent for three seasons.
beats.tells: A staff or volunteer member who shows unusual interest in specific attendees beyond the care role
beats.say: I want to document a concern about a colleague's behavior — can I speak with a supervisor privately?
beats.truth: The most important safeguarding the team does is looking out for each other as much as for attendees.

clips.check: H.O.L.D. — "L" CHECK: "Have I documented the specific behaviors that are making me uncomfortable about this...
clips.move: Name what you see to a supervisor. Document it in writing. The culture of silence is what protects predators in these spaces.
clips.dark_title: Safeguarding In Festival Staff Contexts

clips.name: Compassion Fatigue and Secondary Traumatic Stress

beats.scene: You have supported four difficult situations today — one overdose response, two sexual assault disclosures, one severe psychological crisis.
beats.tells: Emotional numbness in situations that would previously have moved you
beats.say: I need to step out for ten minutes — can someone cover briefly?
beats.truth: You cannot give what you do not have. Your recovery serves the people you are trying to help.

clips.check: C.A.R.E. — "C" CHECK: "Am I actually present with the people I am supporting — or am I performing presence from a...
clips.move: Your recovery is part of the job. Take your breaks. Eat. Drink water. Name what you are carrying. Debrief.
clips.dark_title: Recognizing And Responding To Compassion Fatigue

clips.name: Camp Culture and What Builds It Badly
clips.hook_line: THIS IS HOW WE DO THINGS HERE

beats.hook: THIS IS HOW WE DO THINGS HERE

beats.tells: Privacy norms that function as reporting suppression

beats.truth: The norms you build in calm times define what happens in the hard ones.

clips.name: What You Owe the People Who Run Your Event

beats.scene: Your volunteer briefing says "this is a family" and "we are all in this together." It does not say what the actual shift hours are, what accommodation is provided, what meals are covered, what happens if someone needs to
beats.tells: Volunteer agreements should specify hours, accommodation, meals, and exit terms in writing
beats.say: Here is your written volunteer agreement — read it carefully. Here is how to raise concerns. Here is what I am committed to providing.
beats.truth: Your event runs on the labor of other people. You owe them clarity, safety, and the knowledge that concerns will be heard.

clips.check: E.V.E.N.T. — "N" CHECK: "Do my staff have what they need to do their jobs safely — and do they have a clear path...
clips.move: Provide clear written terms, safe conditions, and a functioning reporting process for every person who works your event.
clips.dark_title: Staff And Volunteer Minimum Standards

clips.name: Fentanyl Strips, Reagent Kits, and Why This Is Non-Optional

beats.scene: "Someone in our camp tested their MDMA Saturday morning and it came back as something completely different." This happens at every major festival.
beats.tells: Fentanyl test strips: dissolve a tiny amount in water, dip — ONE line means fentanyl present, do not use
beats.say: Hold on — let me test it first. I have strips in my kit. Two minutes.
beats.truth: The two minutes it takes to test is not inconvenience. It is the difference between a good night and a medical emergency.

clips.check: S.A.F.E. — "A"CHECK: "Have I tested this — and does everyone in my group know what to do if something goes...
clips.move: Test your stuff. Carry Narcan. Know the overdose signs. These three things save lives.

clips.name: Pedestal Ploy / The Chosen One Setup

beats.scene: "Most women I meet here are just looking for a hook-up.
beats.tells: Compliments that specifically separate you from other women
beats.say: That's really sweet — I'm gonna go check in with my girls. Find me at the set tonight.
beats.truth: A man who needs you to be above other women needs you to be without them. Notice that.

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"O"CHECK: "Where are my women right now — and when did I last actually see them?"
clips.move: Receive the compliment. Stay with your women. Specialness that requires isolation isn't specialness.
clips.dark_title: Other Women Are Your Greatest Safety Asset

clips.name: Peer Coercion / Bro Culture Pressure

beats.scene: "Bro come on, it's one more. You're not gonna go to sleep at 4am at a festival." You're actually done.
beats.tells: Your limit is framed as a character flaw — "soft," "scared," "not a real raver"
beats.say: "I'm tapped — I'm gonna wind down. You lot carry on, I'll catch you at sunrise."
beats.truth: The ones who make you feel weak for having a limit are not your brothers. They're just louder than your gut.

clips.check: B.A.S.S.—"B"CHECK: "What is my body actually saying right now — not what does the group expect me to say?"
clips.move: Your "I'm good" is a complete sentence. The crew that respects it is your actual crew.

clips.name: Hazing as Initiation / Social Proof Pressure
clips.clinical: Social Proof Exploitation / Informed Consent Bypass

beats.scene: "Dude everyone does this here — it's part of the experience.
beats.tells: "Everyone does this" stated as fact — impossible to verify in the moment
beats.say: I'm good for now — I'll figure out my own pace this weekend.
beats.truth: "Everyone does it" is a frame, not a fact. Your judgment is allowed to exist here.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "R" CHECK: "Is this real connection — or performance designed to get me to say yes to something?"
clips.move: Your hesitation is your nervous system working. It doesn't need to be overridden to prove you belong.
clips.dark_title: What Real Festie Culture Actually Looks Like

clips.name: Community Gatekeeping / Identity Policing

beats.scene: "I do not know if this is really your scene — you seem kind of straight-passing." It is said not unkindly but it lands in a familiar tender place.
beats.tells: Your identity, expression, or history is used to question your right to be in a space
beats.say: I am good with who I am — this conversation is not something I need to have.
beats.truth: Queer enough is you, exactly as you are. Anyone else's definition is their limitation, not yours.

clips.check: P.R.I.D.E. — "I" CHECK: "Is my sense of my own identity secure — or am I letting someone else's framework define it...
clips.move: Your identity is valid on your terms, at your level of visibility, in your own timeline. Full stop.
clips.dark_title: Your Identity Is Yours

clips.name: The Hoverer / The Fan Who Becomes a Fixture
clips.hook_line: I JUST LOVE WATCHING YOU CREATE

beats.hook: I JUST LOVE WATCHING YOU CREATE
beats.scene: He's been near your painting station since you set up.
beats.tells: Presence near your workspace extends across the whole weekend without invitation
beats.say: I really appreciate the support — I need to be heads-down for a while. I'll find you when I come up for air.
beats.truth: Admiration that respects your process from a distance is real. Admiration that requires access to your workspace is not admiration.

clips.check: C.R.E.A.T.E. — "T" CHECK: "Who is actually in my creative space right now — and did I invite them there?"
clips.move: Name your workspace boundaries clearly and early. "I go pretty internal while I work" is a complete sentence.
clips.dark_title: Substances And Creative Work — The Vulnerability Window

clips.name: Green Room Access as Grooming / Post-Show Vulnerability

beats.scene: You just came off a set that felt transcendent.
beats.tells: People in backstage spaces you don't know how they got there
beats.say: [To your team before the show]: "30-minute closed cooldown after we come off — then we open the room. Can you hold that?"
beats.truth: The post-show high is real and beautiful. It is also the window people have been waiting all night to exploit.

clips.check: O.U.N.D. — "U" CHECK: "Who is actually in this space — do I know how they got here and what they want?"
clips.move: Land first. Decompress with your core people. Then decide who you want in your space from a clearer head.
clips.dark_title: Green Room Protocol — Yours To Set

clips.name: Peer Guilt Pressure / Inventory Extraction

beats.scene: The vendor two booths over has been friendly all weekend and helped you with a few things.
beats.tells: The "we are family" frame used specifically in commercial transactions
beats.say: I keep my pricing consistent all weekend — I am not able to do discounts. I appreciate you though.
beats.truth: Your margin is your livelihood. Protecting it is not being anti-community. It is being a sustainable business.

clips.check: M.A.R.K.E.T. — "M" CHECK: "Is this exchange actually mutual — or am I absorbing a loss to avoid a social cost?"
clips.move: Your pricing is your pricing. You are allowed to hold it regardless of social pressure.
clips.dark_title: How To Decline Gracefully And Firmly

clips.name: Compassion Fatigue / Giving Until Empty

beats.scene: You are into your third consecutive shift covering for a no-show.
beats.tells: Emotional numbness in situations that would previously have moved you
beats.say: I need to step out for ten minutes — can someone cover the tent briefly?
beats.truth: You cannot give what you do not have. Your recovery is not a luxury. It is the job.

clips.check: H.O.L.D. — "H" CHECK: "Am I actually present with the people I am supporting — or am I running on empty and...
clips.move: Take your breaks. Eat. Drink water. Step outside between difficult interactions. Your depletion serves nobody.
clips.dark_title: Compassion Fatigue Recovery Protocol

clips.name: Confidentiality Weaponized / Organizational Reporting Suppression

beats.scene: You witnessed something that happened between a staff member and a participant that you believe was a violation.
beats.tells: Confidentiality invoked specifically when you try to report staff behavior or organizational failures
beats.say: I understand the confidentiality concern but what I witnessed involves staff behavior that I believe requires escalation. I am going to document it formally.
beats.truth: Confidentiality protects participants. It does not protect organizations from accountability for harm.

clips.check: C.A.R.E. — "A" CHECK: "Is confidentiality being applied to protect the people we serve — or to protect the...
clips.move: Your safeguarding responsibilities include reporting harm you witness — that is not a breach of confidentiality.
clips.dark_title: What To Do When The Reporting Structure Is Broken

clips.name: Founder Syndrome / When Leadership Becomes Ownership

beats.scene: You have run this camp for seven years.
beats.tells: Decisions are made unilaterally and questioning them is received as ingratitude or disloyalty
beats.say: I want to create a formal way for camp members to raise concerns about my decisions and my leadership. Here is what I am proposing.
beats.truth: The camp you built belongs to the community in it as much as to you. Lead accordingly.

clips.check: L.E.A.D. — "E" CHECK: "Am I accountable to my camp in the same ways my camp members are accountable to me?"
clips.move: Build accountability structures that include you. The camp that cannot hold its leader accountable cannot protect its members.
clips.dark_title: Structural Accountability For Camp Leadership

clips.name: Consent Culture That Is Real, Not Decorative

beats.scene: Your event's consent policy is posted at the entrance.
beats.tells: Consent violations handled informally when formal processes exist
beats.say: This person has been reported for a consent violation. Here is our process and here is what happens next regardless of who they are.
beats.truth: A consent policy you do not enforce is not a consent policy. It is a liability.

clips.check: E.V.E.N.T. — "E" CHECK: "Am I enforcing my consent policy consistently — regardless of who the violator is?"
clips.move: Enforce your consent policy consistently. The first exception defines what the policy actually is.
clips.dark_title: What Real Consent Policy Enforcement Looks Like

clips.name: What Not to Mix and Why It Matters

beats.scene: You took MDMA earlier. Someone offers you something they describe as a downer to take the edge off.
beats.tells: MDMA plus alcohol: dramatically increases dehydration and cardiovascular strain
beats.say: What is that exactly? I need to know before I decide — I already took something earlier.
beats.truth: The combination is where most of the risk lives. Know what you are mixing before you mix it.

clips.check: S.A.F.E. — "A" CHECK: "Do I know what I have already taken and do I actually know what I am being offered right...
clips.move: Know what you have taken before taking anything else. When unsure — ask the Harm Reduction tent.
clips.dark_title: Harm Reduction Tent — Use Them For This

clips.name: Scarcity & Urgency / The Closing Window
clips.hook_line: THIS IS ONCE IN A LIFETIME

beats.hook: THIS IS ONCE IN A LIFETIME
beats.scene: "I don't do this for just anyone but there's a private ceremony happening in twenty minutes — only eight people, real medicine holders, you'd have to come right now." He's already walking.
beats.tells: "Right now" / "only tonight" / "this won't happen again"
beats.say: If it's real it can wait two minutes for me to text my camp where I'm going.
beats.truth: Anything that disappears the moment you slow down was never safe to begin with.

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"G"CHECK: "What is my gut saying — and do I have time to text someone where I'm going?"
clips.move: Stop. Breathe. Text someone where you're going. If it evaporates in five minutes — it wasn't real.
clips.dark_title: The Private Ceremony Trap

clips.name: Substance Dependency Grooming

beats.scene: He had the best stuff and he kept finding you.
beats.tells: He is the exclusive source of what you're consuming — no other connects this weekend
beats.say: "I'm good tonight — heading to find my camp. I'll catch you tomorrow."
beats.truth: Your altered state should never be owned by someone who wants something from you.

clips.check: B.A.S.S.—"A"CHECK: "Who controls my access to substances this weekend — and what is that actually costing me?"
clips.move: Know your own source independently of anyone who also wants something from you.
clips.dark_title: When The Supply Is The Setup

clips.name: The Guardian Who Isn't / Exploiting Overwhelm

beats.scene: You got separated from your group Saturday night and your phone died.
beats.tells: Appears at peak vulnerability: separated, lost, depleted, frightened
beats.say: Thank you so much — that was genuinely kind. I'm going to try to find my camp now. Can you point me toward the Rangers?
beats.truth: Real help returns you to independence. Watch for that.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "V" CHECK: "Does this person's help return me to my own people and navigation — or keep me...
clips.move: Accept real help gratefully. Return to your own people as soon as you're able. Gratitude is not a contract.
clips.dark_title: Dead Phone = Highest Risk Window

clips.name: Your Identity Used Against You

beats.scene: You ended things with him Saturday morning.
beats.tells: Implicit or explicit references to "people back home" or your non-festival life when you exercise independence
beats.say: What you are doing is harassment and I am going to report it. I suggest you stop.
beats.truth: Your identity is yours to share on your terms. Anyone who tries to use it against you is committing a harm.

clips.check: P.R.I.D.E. — "I" CHECK: "Is this person treating private information I shared with care — or as something they hold...
clips.move: Document it. Report it to festival staff. Tell someone you trust. You do not have to manage this alone.
clips.dark_title: If You Are Being Threatened With Outing

clips.name: Sexual Attention as Artistic Validation

beats.scene: He's been complimenting your work genuinely all weekend — knowledgeable, specific, clearly understands what you're doing.
beats.tells: Artistic interest and sexual interest arrive in the same package from the same person
beats.say: I'm going to keep those two things separate — I'm glad you connected with the work. I'm not available for the rest.
beats.truth: Your art being beautiful does not make your body available. Full stop.

clips.check: C.R.E.A.T.E. — "T" CHECK: "Is the appreciation of my work actually about my work — or is it cover for something...
clips.move: Receive genuine artistic recognition with full confidence. Decline sexual interest without apology. These are completely separate.
clips.dark_title: Your Work Being Shared Is Not Your Body Being Available

clips.name: When Admiration Becomes Stalking

beats.scene: She's been at six of your shows in three cities.
beats.tells: Attendance at multiple shows in multiple cities without your invitation
beats.say: [To your tour manager]: "I need you to document this person's appearances and pull their backstage access. I want a record."
beats.truth: "Dedicated fan" is not a category that overrides your safety. Your discomfort is data.

clips.check: S.O.U.N.D. — "D" CHECK: "Have I documented this person's behavior with dates, locations, and screenshots — sol...
clips.move: Trust your body's signal. Document. Tell your team. Report early.
clips.dark_title: Documenting And Reporting Stalking

clips.name: Romantic Entanglement With Access Holders
clips.hook_line: I CAN GET YOU IN ANYWHERE

beats.hook: I CAN GET YOU IN ANYWHERE
beats.scene: You met him at the winter market and the connection was real.
beats.tells: Romantic relationship develops with someone who controls your business access
beats.say: I am going to apply to this one directly — I want to build my own relationship with the organizer.
beats.truth: Your business access is yours. It should never live inside someone else's hands.

clips.check: M.A.R.K.E.T. — "A" CHECK: "Does my business access depend on this relationship — and what does that mean for...
clips.move: Keep your professional relationships independent of your romantic ones. Build your own circuit reputation.
clips.dark_title: Building Access Independent Of Any One Person

clips.name: When Your Support Role Gets Exploited
clips.hook_line: THE PARTICIPANT WHO MANIPULATES YOUR CARE

beats.hook: THE PARTICIPANT WHO MANIPULATES YOUR CARE
beats.scene: He has been to the Harm Reduction tent four times this weekend.
beats.tells: Multiple visits with shifting or evolving presentations of their support need
beats.say: I want to flag something I have noticed about a repeated visitor — can we talk privately for a minute?
beats.truth: Your care role requires discernment as much as compassion. Both are part of doing it well.

clips.check: H.O.L.D. — "O" CHECK: "Is the pattern of this person's engagement consistent with genuine support seeking — or...
clips.move: Trust the pattern. Name it to a colleague. Document it. That is what good safeguarding looks like.
clips.dark_title: What To Do When Something Feels Off

clips.name: Being Blamed for Systemic Failures

beats.scene: A participant had a serious adverse event during your shift.
beats.tells: Post-incident debrief focuses on your actions rather than the systemic conditions you were placed in
beats.say: I want to cooperate fully with any review. I am also going to document my own account of what happened and what conditions I was working in.
beats.truth: You are responsible for your actions. You are not responsible for the systemic conditions you were placed in.

clips.check: C.A.R.E. — "A" CHECK: "Have I documented my own account of events immediately — before organizational framing...
clips.move: Write your account immediately. Do not sign anything before reading it against your own record.
clips.dark_title: Protecting Yourself After An Incident

clips.name: When What You Provide Becomes Control

beats.scene: You provided accommodation and festival access to six members of your camp.
beats.tells: Members whose accommodation or access you control behave differently from those who are independent
beats.say: Your place here is not conditional on agreeing with me. I want to be clear about that and I want you to feel free to push back.
beats.truth: Generosity that creates dependency is not generosity. It is leverage that happens to be warm.

clips.check: L.E.A.D. — "A" CHECK: "Do the members who depend most on what I provide feel the most or least free to push...
clips.move: Acknowledge the leverage your resources create and actively work against it rather than ignoring it.
clips.dark_title: Managing Resource Dependency Ethically

clips.name: What You Actually Own From Your Event

beats.scene: Your festival set videos are performing well on your YouTube channel.
beats.tells: Sweeping recording rights clauses in standard booking confirmation language
beats.say: Here is what we record at our events and how we use it. Here is how we share revenue with performing artists.
beats.truth: The content that builds your brand was created by artists. Treat their contribution accordingly.

clips.check: E.V.E.N.T. — "V" CHECK: "Are the artists whose recordings I am using being compensated fairly for the commercial...
clips.move: Be transparent about what you record, how you use it, and share revenue with the people who created it.
clips.dark_title: Ethical Recording Rights Practice

clips.name: Overdose Response and Getting Help Without Fear

beats.scene: Your campmate is not responsive.
beats.tells: Unresponsive or very difficult to rouse — this is the clearest emergency sign
beats.say: "Someone is unresponsive — I need medical help at [your location] right now!" Then do not hang up.
beats.truth: The call you make in the next 60 seconds is the difference. Make it.

clips.check: S.A.F.E. — "F" CHECK: "Do I know where the medical tent is and do I have Narcan in my camp right now?"
clips.move: Call for help first. Narcan second. Recovery position third. Stay with them. Do not leave.
clips.dark_title: The 60-Second Overdose Response Protocol

clips.name: PLUR Weaponized / Your Boundary Is the Bad Vibe

beats.scene: "I thought you were an open person." Said softly.
beats.tells: Your "no" is reframed as your trauma, ego, or fear — not a valid decision
beats.say: My boundaries are part of my healing too. I'm good with my decision.
beats.truth: Real PLUR means your no is honored without a negotiation. The end.

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"G"CHECK: "What is my body saying — separate from the story his words are telling me?"
clips.move: Trust the body over the frame. If it felt like pressure, it was pressure — regardless of vocabulary used.
clips.dark_title: The Consent Culture Predator

clips.name: Intermittent Reinforcement / The Pull-Push Cycle

beats.scene: Friday she was electric — connected, present, making you feel like the only person at the festival.
beats.tells: Intense warmth followed by unexplained withdrawal, then warmth again
beats.say: [To yourself]: "I deserve warmth that doesn't come with cold attached to manage me."
beats.truth: Consistency is not boring. Unpredictability is not chemistry — it's a mechanism.

clips.check: B.A.S.S. — "B" CHECK: "Am I feeling relief or genuine happiness when she's warm? Those are different things."
clips.move: Notice whether you feel relief or joy when the warmth returns. Relief is not connection. Relief is a warning.
clips.dark_title: This Is Not Just A Romance Thing

clips.name: Festival Time Distortion / False Familiarity

beats.scene: It's Saturday night and you feel like you've known these people your whole life.
beats.tells: You feel closer to someone after 48 hours than to people you've known for years
beats.say: "I'm feeling this — let's stay in touch after the festival and see what this looks like in the regular world."
beats.truth: Real connection survives the end of the festival. Manufactured connection requires the festival bubble to sustain it.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "E" CHECK: "Everyone here is still a stranger to me — warmth and familiarity are not the same as safety."
clips.move: Let the connection be real. Don't let the speed be set by the environment rather than you.
clips.dark_title: The 72-Hour Rule For First-Timers

clips.name: Assumed Safety in Queer Spaces / False Sanctuaries

beats.scene: The tent has a progress pride flag and the DJ is playing music you know from queer spaces.
beats.tells: You are less alert in a space because it is coded as queer or LGBTQ-friendly
beats.say: Is this a space you know? Who runs it and are they solid?
beats.truth: Safety is not an aesthetic. Verify through behavior and community relationships, not flags and decor.

clips.check: P.R.I.D.E. — "D" CHECK: "Have I verified that this space is actually safer — or am I assuming based on aesthetics?"
clips.move: Let queer-coded spaces be a warm starting point. Verify actual safety through behavior and relationships.
clips.dark_title: What Makes A Space Actually Safer

clips.name: Scope Creep / Moving Goalposts on the Brief
clips.hook_line: WE JUST NEED THIS ONE THING

beats.hook: WE JUST NEED THIS ONE THING
beats.scene: "We love the direction — can you also just add a panel on the left?
beats.tells: New requests arrive after previous work is completed and your investment is high
beats.say: That's a new element outside the original brief — happy to include it, my rate for additions is [X]. Want to proceed?
beats.truth: Your time and skill are finite. Scope creep is not creative collaboration — it's extraction in slow motion.

clips.check: C.R.E.A.T.E. — "C" CHECK: "Is what I'm being asked to do now what I agreed to do — and is the compensation still...
clips.move: Changes to scope trigger a new compensation conversation. Every time. Without apology.
clips.dark_title: The Change Order Conversation

clips.name: How Touring Disconnects You From Everyone Who Knows You

beats.scene: You're four weeks into a run and you haven't had a real conversation with anyone from home in two weeks.
beats.tells: Your home support network feels increasingly remote and unreachable
beats.say: [To your most trusted person at home]: "Can we do a weekly call on Sundays for the duration of this run? I need someone external to check in with."
beats.truth: The road is a closed system. Keep one door open to the outside.

clips.check: O.U.N.D. — "U" CHECK: "When did I last have a real conversation with someone who knew me before the music?"
clips.move: Maintain active connection to your home network throughout the tour. Schedule it.
clips.dark_title: Maintaining Connection On The Road

clips.name: When Your Road Partner Controls the Vehicle or Money

beats.scene: You share a van and travel costs with her.
beats.tells: One partner controls transportation and the other is fully dependent on it for the circuit
beats.say: I am really excited to do this together — let us get the basic terms in writing so we are both protected.
beats.truth: The partnership that starts as family needs the same paperwork as a business partnership. Because it is both.

clips.check: M.A.R.K.E.T. — "A" CHECK: "Do I have independent access to the money and transportation in this arrangement?"
clips.move: Never enter a traveling vendor partnership without a written agreement covering money, transport, and exit.
clips.dark_title: Traveling Vendor Partnership Agreement Basics

clips.name: Being Kept Too Depleted to See Clearly

beats.scene: By Saturday afternoon you have been on since 6am, you have not had a proper meal, the staff communication channel is so full of urgent requests that you have stopped reading it, and the supervisor you would report concer
beats.tells: Staffing is so thin that there is never a moment to observe, think, or raise concerns
beats.say: "I need to take my break before I can cover anything else — where can I get food?"
beats.truth: A depleted volunteer is not a martyr. A depleted volunteer is a liability for everyone including the people they are trying to protect.

clips.check: H.O.L.D. — "H" CHECK: "Do I have the basic resources I need to do this role safely — food, sleep, breaks, a...
clips.move: Meet your own basic needs first. You cannot report-effectively from a place of complete depletion.
clips.dark_title: When The Reporting Structure Is Broken

clips.name: Processing What You Carry So It Does Not Carry You

beats.scene: The shift ends and the tendency is to immediately transition back to the festival or to crash into sleep.
beats.tells: Name the hardest thing from the shift out loud to at least one colleague before leaving
beats.say: Before we all head out — can we take ten minutes to say what today was like? I need to name some of it out loud.
beats.truth: What you name, you can put down. What you do not name, you carry. Name it.

clips.check: C.A.R.E. — "E" CHECK: "Have I actually stopped and named what I am carrying from this shift — or am I pushing...
clips.move: Name what was hard. Out loud. To someone. Before you leave the tent. That is the minimum.

clips.name: When Camp Membership Becomes a Control Structure
clips.clinical: High Control Group Dynamics / BITE Model

beats.scene: You care deeply about your camp and your members.
beats.tells: Leaving the camp carries significant social cost — former members are characterized negatively
beats.say: "I want to make sure our camp is a place people feel genuinely free in — including free to leave, free to question, and free to talk to outsiders."
beats.truth: A community that requires control to maintain cohesion is not a community. It is a structure.

clips.check: L.E.A.D. — "L" CHECK: "Can members of my camp leave freely, talk to outsiders freely, and question decisions freely...
clips.move: Examine your camp honestly against these criteria. Make changes where the examination reveals them.
clips.dark_title: The Bite Model — A Self-Assessment Tool

clips.name: Practical Standards for Honest Event Production

beats.scene: The promoters you respect — the ones whose names on a lineup or a market mean something — have all built reputations over time through the same things: they pay what they agreed.
beats.tells: Written agreements with all artists, vendors, and staff before any money changes hands
beats.say: Here is our event agreement. Here is our safety plan. Here is how to raise concerns. Here is when payment will arrive.
beats.truth: Ethical event production is not complicated. It is a set of choices you make consistently. Make them.

clips.check: E.V.E.N.T. — "T" CHECK: "Would the artists, vendors, and staff who worked my last event describe it the way I would...
clips.move: Run the checklist before and after every event. The reputation you build is the one that is accurate.
clips.dark_title: The Ethical Promoter Checklist

clips.name: How to Actually Intervene When Something Looks Wrong

beats.scene: You are walking between stages and you see a woman sitting with a man who seems agitated.
beats.tells: THE DISTRACTION: walk up like you know her — "Oh my god, there you are! I have been looking everywhere for you!"
beats.say: Oh my god, there you are! I have been looking everywhere — come on, everyone is at the stage.
beats.truth: You do not need to be certain. You need to be the person who showed up.

clips.check: S.A.F.E. —"S" CHECK: "What did I actually see — and which of the three moves fits this situation?"
clips.move: Pick one of the three moves and do it. Doing something imperfectly is always better than doing nothing perfectly.
clips.dark_title: Reading A Situation Quickly

clips.name: The Substance Gatekeeper / The Plug Who Owns You

beats.scene: He found you Thursday night and what he had made the music feel like it lived inside your ribcage.
beats.tells: He is the exclusive or primary source of what you're consuming all weekend
beats.say: I'm good for tonight — heading to find my camp. I'll catch you at the set tomorrow.
beats.truth: Your consciousness is yours. Nobody gets to be the gatekeeper of your inner world.

clips.check: G.R.O.V.E.—"G"CHECK: "What is my body telling me about this person — separate from what they're providing me?"
clips.move: Know your own supply or know your source independently of anyone who also wants something from you.

clips.name: Cult Dynamics in Men's Circles / False Brotherhood Hierarchy

beats.scene: The men's circle Saturday morning cracked something open in you.
beats.tells: Leader is always the most evolved person in the room — hierarchy is fixed
beats.say: That sounds powerful — I need to sit with it before I commit. Can I reach you in a week?
beats.truth: Real brotherhood points you toward your own authority. Predatory brotherhood points you toward theirs.

clips.check: B.A.S.S. — "S" CHECK: "When did I last check in with my own people — not this circle, not this leader, but MY people?"
clips.move: Receive genuine value. Take the pitch home. Verify with people outside the circle before spending anything.
clips.dark_title: How To Spot A Predatory Men's Leader

clips.name: Targeting You When You're Most Depleted

beats.scene: It's 3am Saturday and you're exhausted, slightly lost, slightly overwhelmed, and running on whatever you took six hours ago.
beats.tells: You're at peak overwhelm, exhaustion, or disorientation when they appear
beats.say: I need to find my camp and sleep — if I'm not better in the morning this can wait.
beats.truth: Decisions made at your most depleted are not your decisions. They're the depletion's decisions.

clips.check: R.A.V.E. — "A" CHECK: "Am I making decisions right now with the same judgment I'd have at 2pm on a Tuesday? If...
clips.move: Know your vulnerable windows. Pre-plan support for them. Don't make major decisions inside them.
clips.dark_title: The Predicted Hard Moments At Your First Festival

clips.name: The Visibility of Queer Relationships in Festival Contexts
clips.hook_line: RELATIONSHIP PRESSURE IN A SMALL COMMUNITY

beats.hook: RELATIONSHIP PRESSURE IN A SMALL COMMUNITY
beats.scene: You tried to end things with her Saturday morning but she knows everyone in the queer camp you are both staying in.
